docs: The account that will be set as the program owner
This account pays for initialization and will have administrative privileges

accounts.name: redeemer_config
docs: Redeemer Config account, which saves program data useful for other
instructions, specifically for inbound transfers. Also saves the payer
of the [`initialize`](crate::initialize) instruction as the program's
owner.

accounts.name: token_bridge_config
docs: Token Bridge config. Token Bridge program needs this account to
invoke the Wormhole program to post messages. Even though it is a
required account for redeeming token transfers, it is not actually
used for completing these transfers.

accounts.name: token_bridge_custody_signer
docs: data; it is purely just a signer for Token Bridge SPL tranfers.

accounts.name: token_bridge_mint_authority
docs: data; it is purely just a signer (SPL mint authority) for Token Bridge
wrapped assets.

accounts.name: token_bridge_emitter
docs: that holds data; it is purely just a signer for posting Wormhole
messages on behalf of the Token Bridge program.

accounts.name: wormhole_fee_collector
docs: Wormhole fee collector account, which requires lamports before the
program can post a message (if there is a fee). Token Bridge program
handles the fee payments.

accounts.name: token_bridge_sequence
docs: Token Bridge emitter's sequence account. Like with all Wormhole
emitters, this account keeps track of the sequence number of the last
posted message.

types.name: DepositExecuted
docs: Emitted when a cross-chain deposit is executed into a vault.

docs: The recipient account that initiated the deposit

fields.name: vault_address
docs: The vault where tokens were deposited

fields.name: amount
docs: The amount of tokens deposited

fields.name: token_mint
docs: The mint address of the deposited token

fields.name: wormhole_message_hash
docs: The hash of the Wormhole message that triggered this deposit

fields.name: timestamp
docs: Unix timestamp when the deposit was executed

types.name: DepositReturned
docs: Emitted when a deposit is returned to the original sender.
This happens when a deposit cannot be processed or is rejected.

docs: The recipient account receiving the returned tokens

fields.name: vault_address
docs: The vault address that rejected the deposit

fields.name: amount
docs: The amount of tokens returned

fields.name: token_mint
docs: The mint address of the returned token

fields.name: timestamp
docs: Unix timestamp when the deposit was returned

fields.name: amount_wrapped

fields.name: token_wrapped
docs: The wrapped token mint address

fields.name: amount_unwrapped
docs: The amount of unwrapped (native) tokens received

fields.name: token_unwrapped
docs: The unwrapped (native) token mint address

fields.name: a_to_b
docs: Direction of the swap (true if A to B, false if B to A)

fields.name: destination

fields.name: timestamp

fields.name: config
docs: Token Bridge config account

fields.name: custody_signer
docs: Token Bridge custody signer PDA

fields.name: mint_authority
docs: Token Bridge mint authority PDA

types.name: ReceivedDeposit
docs: Represents a cross-chain deposit received via Wormhole.
This account tracks the status of deposits coming from other chains,
storing the necessary information to process them into Solana vaults.

fields.name: wormhole_message_hash
docs: Hash of the Wormhole VAA message that triggered this deposit

fields.name: amount
docs: Amount of tokens being deposited

fields.name: token_mint
docs: Mint address of the token being deposited

fields.name: recipient
docs: Recipient address that should receive the deposit or shares

fields.name: vault_address
docs: Target vault address for the deposit

fields.name: processed
docs: Whether the deposit has been processed

fields.name: nonce
docs: Unique nonce for this transaction

fields.name: source_chain
docs: Chain ID of the source chain

fields.name: source_address
docs: Address on the source chain that initiated the deposit

fields.name: timestamp
docs: Unix timestamp when the deposit was received

types.name: Redeemer
docs: Central authority account for the Wormhole relayer program.
Manages cross-chain deposit processing, reentrancy protection,
and fee configuration for the relayer service.

fields.name: owner
docs: Owner/authority of the redeemer

fields.name: bump
docs: PDA bump seed

fields.name: token_bridge
docs: Token Bridge addresses for cross-chain operations

fields.name: processing_fee_bps
docs: Processing fee in basis points (e.g., 100 = 1%)

fields.name: is_processing
docs: Reentrancy guard to prevent concurrent processing

types.name: RedeemerFeeSet
docs: Emitted when the redeemer fee percentage is updated.

fields.name: fee_bps
docs: The new fee in basis points (e.g., 100 = 1%)

fields.name: timestamp
docs: Unix timestamp when the fee was set

fields.name: token_bridge_wrapped_mint
docs: The wrapped token mint from the token bridge

fields.name: relayer_token_account
docs: The relayer's main token account

fields.name: relayer_fee_token_account
docs: The relayer's fee collection token account

types.name: TokenReceived

fields.name: recipient

fields.name: vault_address
docs: The target vault address for the deposit

fields.name: amount
docs: The amount of tokens received

fields.name: fee_amount
docs: The fee amount deducted from the received tokens

fields.name: token_mint
docs: The mint address of the received token

fields.name: wormhole_message_hash
docs: The hash of the Wormhole message that triggered this event

fields.name: timestamp
docs: Unix timestamp when the tokens were received

types.name: UserRole
docs: User role account that tracks a specific role assignment.
This account represents the assignment of a specific role to a specific user.
The account address is derived as a PDA from the user's public key and the role ID.

fields.name: has_role
docs: Whether the user has the role (true) or not (false)

types.name: Vault
docs: The main vault state that manages user deposits, withdrawals, and strategy allocations.
This struct represents a tokenized vault that:
- Accepts deposits in an underlying token
- Issues shares representing vault ownership
- Allocates funds to various investment strategies
- Manages fees and profit distribution
- Enforces access controls and limits

fields.name: last_fee_accrual_ts
docs: Last time (unix ts) a streaming-fee inflation was applied.

fields.name: management_fee_rate
docs: Annual management-fee rate, fixed-point with 1e7 precision.

fields.name: pending_management_fee_rate
docs: Pending management fee rate that will take effect after the time delay

fields.name: fee_update_time
docs: Timestamp when the pending fee rate should take effect

types.name: VaultWhitelist
docs: Maintains a whitelist of approved vaults, source chains, and source addresses
for enhanced security in cross-chain operations.
This account provides security controls to limit which vaults can receive
cross-chain deposits and from which chains or addresses deposits can originate.
When empty, all vaults/chains/addresses are allowed; when populated, only
explicitly whitelisted entities can interact with the system.

fields.name: authority
docs: The authority that can manage the whitelist

fields.name: bump
docs: PDA bump seed

fields.name: validate_source_chains
docs: Whether to validate source chains
If true, only chains in allowed_source_chains will be accepted

fields.name: validate_source_addresses
docs: Whether to validate source addresses
If true, only addresses in allowed_source_addresses will be accepted

fields.name: whitelisted_vaults
docs: List of whitelisted vaults (addresses that can receive deposits)
If empty, all vaults are allowed; if populated, only listed vaults can receive deposits

fields.name: allowed_source_chains
docs: List of allowed source chains (Wormhole chain IDs)
If empty, all chains are allowed; if populated, only listed chains can send deposits

fields.name: allowed_source_addresses
docs: List of allowed source addresses (32-byte addresses from source chains)
If empty, all addresses are allowed; if populated, only listed addresses can send deposits
